chunks: In a report of Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: It is not befitting for the Muslim man to establish brotherhood with the immoral person, for indeed he adorns his own deed to him, and he desires that he be like him, and he will not help him in the affairs of his worldly life, nor the affairs of his Hereafter; and his entry to him and his departure from his presence are a disgrace upon him.

key_terms.الْفَاجِرَ: The fajir: one who commits open immorality, violates the bounds of God; distinct from kafir (disbeliever) but morally corrupt
key_terms.شَيْنٌ: Disgrace, blemish, shame; antonym of zain (beauty, adornment)
key_terms.مَعَاد: The place/time of return; refers to the Hereafter and one's ultimate return to God
key_terms.يُزَيِّنُ: To adorn, beautify, make something appear attractive; used often of Satan beautifying sin
key_terms.يُوَاخِيَ: To establish brotherhood (mu'akhat); refers to the formal or informal bond of brotherhood in Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about befriending immoral people in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), as narrated through Imam al-Sadiq, forbids a Muslim from forging close friendship or brotherhood with a morally corrupt person (fajir). The teaching provides three reasons: the corrupt person beautifies his own sinful conduct in the Muslim's eyes, wishes the Muslim to become like him, and provides no benefit in this world or the next. Furthermore, merely being seen coming and going from such a person's company is itself a source of shame and social disgrace for the Muslim. This saying addressed the early Muslim community's need to maintain the integrity of their social ties and guard against moral corruption through association.

en.hubeali:
And in a report of Abdul A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting for the Muslim man that he establishes brotherhood with the immoral one for he would decorate his own deed to him, and he would love it if he would happen to be like him, and he would not assist him upon the matter of his world, nor a matter of his Hereafter; and his entry and his exit from his presence would be a disgrace upon him’.
en.sarwar: 2. In the Hadith of ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) it is said that

Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) said: “It is not proper for a Muslim man to become a friend of an indecent person; he tries to make his deeds seem attractive to him and loves that one to behave like him (indecent). He does not assist him in his religious matters or the matters of the hereafter. The coming and going of an indecent person is a disgrace to one.”
